vilayet_stats.source: Sum of all Edirne-vilayet clusters = Filibe+İslimye mapped total (929,929) + Edirne/Tekfurdağı/Gelibolu mapped total (911,351). The unadjusted official bases are in the 'official' rows.

Tahrir-i cedid register BOA Y.EE 34/48 = Salname-i Vilayet-i Edirne def. 7 (1293), pp.113-114: 464,271 males (171,777 Muslim + 16,353 Muslim Kıpti; 265,335 Rum/Bulgar, 953 Armenian, 3,642 Catholic, 3,308 Christian Kıpti, 2,903 Jews), doubled as in A. Koyuncu, Avrasya Etüdleri 44 (2013), Tables 4-5.

Official register above minus 5,806 Jews. Muslims x1.378 in Hasköy and Yanbolu kazas (McCarthy 1995: 432,303 Muslims in Eastern Rumelia against 313,620 registered). Muslims x0.75 in Zağra-i Atik, Çırpan and Kızanlık, and x0.85 in Karinâbâd, Aydos, Burgaz, Ahyolu and Misivri, to meet the author's calibration targets.

Ubicini & Pavet de Courteille, État présent de l'Empire ottoman (1876), p.91: 557,692 Muslims + 45,418 Muslim Roma; 937,054 Rum/Bulgar, 16,194 Armenians, 12,144 Catholics, 9,252 Christian Roma; 16,432 Jews. The Filibe/İslimye part of this series matches the older 1290-92 salname count (353,779 males), not the 1875-76 tahrir.

vilayet_stats.vilayet: Edirne – Edirne, Tekfurdağı, Gelibolu sancakları (official, derived)
vilayet_stats.source: Ubicini 1876 vilayet totals minus twice the 1290-92 salname Filibe+İslimye males (130,529 Muslim, 13,743 Kıpti, 209,507 non-Muslim; Koyuncu 2013 Table 3). Non-Muslims include about 10,626 Jews. Distributed to kazas by the FO 881/3655 village counts (Köse 2019, Tables 6, 9, 10) plus town estimates.

vilayet_stats.vilayet: Edirne – Edirne, Tekfurdağı, Gelibolu sancakları (as mapped)
vilayet_stats.source: Derived official residual minus Jews. Muslims x1.378 (McCarthy-type correction) in the Dimetoka, Çirmen-Mustafapaşa and Kızılağaç kazas and in the Edirne-kaza villages.

vilayet_stats.vilayet: Selanik – Drama sancağı part (Yenice-i Karasu, İskeçe, Darıdere)
vilayet_stats.source: Male counts, doubled: Yenice-i Karasu 9,533 Muslim / 2,738 Christian; Eskice-İskeçe 867 / 3,853; Darıdere 20,139 / 162. From the 1873 bedel-i askerî register as published in Ethnographie des vilayets d'Andrinople, de Monastir et de Salonique (1878) and Layard FO 881/3655 (Köse 2019 Table 40).
Çatalca special district (57,957 without Jews) + European side of Dersaadet (680,000), rows below.
Ottoman census 1881/82-1893 in K. Karpat, IJMES 9 (1978): Çatalca kaza 18,313, Silivri 18,333 (965 Jews), Büyükçekmece 22,276. Mapped without Jews: 57,957.

Ministry of Interior 1885 figure (Karpat 1978, Table 1): 384,910 Muslims, 359,412 non-Muslim subjects, 129,243 foreigners; 44,361 Jews. The map uses only the European side, about 680,000 people without Jews, at about 46% Muslim. No district breakdown was found, so the split between districts is estimated.

sources: Aşkın Koyuncu, '1877-1878 Osmanlı-Rus Harbi Öncesinde Şarkî Rumeli Nüfusu', Avrasya Etüdleri 44 (2013/2): 177-208 (dergipark article-file 422104). Tables 4-5 give male counts by millet for every kaza, town and nahiye of the Filibe and İslimye sanjaks, from the tahrir-i cedid register BOA Y.EE 34/48 and the Salname-i Vilayet-i Edirne def. 7 (1293), pp.113-114. Table 3 gives the 1290-92 salnames. Footnotes cite McCarthy's and Ömer Turan's Muslim estimates.

Justin McCarthy, Death and Exile (1995), pp.108-110, via Koyuncu 2013 n.51: 432,303 Muslims in Eastern Rumelia and 1,069,580 in the Danube vilayet in 1877. Used as the upper bound of the Muslim under-registration correction (432,303 / 313,620 registered = x1.378).
Ömer Turan, The Turkish Minority in Bulgaria 1878-1908 (TTK 1998), via Koyuncu: about 400,000 Muslims in Eastern Rumelia and 1,200,000 in the Danube vilayet. Used for comparison.

Muhammed Köse, 'İngiliz Büyükelçisi A. H. Layard'ın Raporuna Göre 1878 Yılında Türkiye Avrupası'nın Demografik Yapısı', Trakya Üniv. Edebiyat Fak. Dergisi 9/18 (2019): 236-291 (dergipark 772716). FO 881/3655 village counts (Muslim / Çingene / non-Muslim males) for every kaza of the Edirne, Tekfurdağı and Gelibolu sanjaks (Tables 6, 9, 10) and the Drama sanjak (Table 40).

A. Ubicini & A. Pavet de Courteille, État présent de l'Empire ottoman (Paris 1876), p.91, from the 1293 salname: Edirne vilayet 1,594,186 (603,110 Muslims incl. 45,418 Muslim Roma; 974,644 Christians; 16,432 Jews). Cited via English Wikipedia 'Adrianople vilayet'.

Kemal H. Karpat, 'Ottoman Population Records and the Census of 1881/82-1893', IJMES 9 (1978): 237-274. Çatalca special district by kaza; Istanbul 1885 (384,910 Muslims, 359,412 non-Muslim subjects, 129,243 foreigners); Edirne province in 1893 by sanjak.

K. Karpat, Ottoman Population 1830-1914 (1985), pp.251-257, via Kaya Göktepe, Trakya Üniv. Sosyal Bilimler Dergisi 16/2 (2014) (dergipark 321363): 1877-78 male totals by sanjak (Edirne 190,585; Tekfurdağı 49,751; Gelibolu 58,361; Filibe 266,088; İslimye 87,691). Used as a cross-check.
Belleten (TTK), full text no. 102 (belleten.gov.tr/tam-metin/102): Edirne city had 94,000 people in 1858 (35,000 Muslim Turks, 59,000 non-Muslims) and 74,000 in 1882 (20,000 Muslims).

M. Kiprovska & M. Kiel, 'Kırcaali', TDV İslâm Ansiklopedisi: Kırcaali belonged to Hasköy kaza until 1885, when it became a kaza of 101 villages, almost all with Turkish names. The 1287 salname gives Hasköy kaza 23,467 Muslim and 18,461 Christian males.

Ethnographie des vilayets d'Andrinople, de Monastir et de Salonique (Constantinople 1878; archive.org scan), from the 1873 bedel-i askerî register. Used for the nahiye structure of Edirne kaza (Üsküdar, Ada, Çöke, Manastır) and, via Layard, for the Drama-sanjak kazas. It was compiled by the Bulgarian Exarchate (M. Kusev, G. Gruev), so it is register-based but not a Turkish source.
R. J. More, Under the Balkans (London 1877), via Wikipedia/G. Demeter: Filibe sanjak by kaza (about 3,700 Greek males in Filibe kaza). Used for the Greek share of Christians.
Carl Sax 1878 ethnographic map and Stanford's 1877 Ethnological Map (from the draft). Used for placing groups within districts only.

Author-supplied 1875 targets for the share of ethnic Bulgarians in each modern Bulgarian oblast. Clusters were assigned to oblasts by their centres, using github.com/yurukov/Bulgaria-geocoding provinces.geojson.
caveats: CALIBRATION CONFLICT. The Ottoman registers alone do not reproduce the author's oblast targets. Bulgarian share with registers only vs target: Haskovo 53.8 vs 42, Yambol 65.6 vs 60, Stara Zagora 65.3 vs 75, Burgas 46.7 vs 54. Plovdiv 61.9, Pazardzhik 71.6, Sliven 65.8, Smolyan 34.0 and Kardzhali 4.1 were already within ±5. To meet the four outliers I raised Muslims in Haskovo/Yambol-area kazas (McCarthy upper bound, x1.378) and lowered them below the register in Stara Zagora kazas (x0.75) and Burgas kazas (x0.85). The lowering contradicts the 1875-76 register and the Ottoman-first source policy. It was done only because the author asked for these targets, and each cluster's groups text records it. I set the calibrated oblasts at the edge of the ±5 band closest to the register: Stara Zagora 70.7, Burgas 49.4, Haskovo 46.1, Smolyan 34.0.

The McCarthy factor x1.378 is his Eastern Rumelia total against the register, so it is an upper bound. It was applied only in the Hasköy, Yanbolu, Kızılağaç, Çirmen-Mustafapaşa and Dimetoka kazas and the Edirne-kaza villages. Muslims of the future Eastern Rumelia in this map total about 320,000, well under McCarthy's 432,303.

The oblast check uses cluster centres and only this region's clusters. Sofia oblast has just Koprivshtitsa here (95% Bulgarian); the rest of it is in the Tuna dataset. Tuna-dataset clusters inside Burgas oblast (Luda Kamchia) and Sliven oblast (Kotel) were not counted.

The total for the Edirne, Tekfurdağı and Gelibolu sanjaks (886,628) is derived by subtraction. It assumes that Ubicini's 1293 series carried the older 1290-92 Filibe/İslimye counts; Koyuncu notes that the 1294-95 Devlet salnames repeat them. The FO 881/3655 counts cover villages only and come from older salnames. The lists for Çorlu (39 villages) and Kırkkilise (31 villages) look incomplete. Town populations (Edirne city etc.), the Saray and Midye kazas, and the Tırnovacık nahiye (24,000 Christians) are my estimates, scaled to fit inside the official residual.

How each kaza is split among its clusters, and the Turk/Pomak split, are my estimates. Muslim Roma (Kıpti) follow the register, and all are counted as muslim_other. For towns in the Edirne/Tekfurdağı/Gelibolu sanjaks, Roma are set at about 13% of Muslims, derived from the Ubicini residual.

Darıdere kaza (Drama sanjak) is assumed to cover Zlatograd, Eğridere/Ardino and the northern Xanthi Pomak plateau; the Eğridere assignment is uncertain. Koşukavak is put in Gümülcine kaza and Kırcaali in Hasköy kaza (TDV).
The İskeçe town figure (only 18% Muslim) comes from the Exarchate-compiled 1873 register. It may undercount Muslims, but it was kept because it is the only register figure available.

Istanbul European side: about 680,000 (without Jews) is my estimate. The 1885 census gives no district breakdown that I could find, and it already includes post-1877 Muslim refugees. The Çatalca figures (1881/82-93) are also post-war.
Jews are excluded everywhere and the three shares renormalised. Cluster populations are rounded; kaza sums match the corrected register within a few persons.
New or moved points (Klisura, Koprivshtitsa, Chepelare, Bachkovo–Hvoyna, Echinos, Termes–Oraio) were placed by hand. All are inland, but they were not re-run through the 1 km land mask.
changes: POPULATION added to all 142 clusters (region total 2,653,821; Jews excluded). Filibe & İslimye: 1875-76 tahrir / 1293 salname male counts x2 for 21 kaza, town and nahiye units (Koyuncu T4-5). Edirne/Tekfurdağı/Gelibolu: FO 881/3655 village counts x2 plus towns, Saray, Midye and Tırnovacık, scaled to the Ubicini 1293 residual (Muslims x0.99, Christians x1.027). Drama-sanjak kazas: 1873 register x2. Çatalca: 1881/82-93 census. Istanbul European side: 680,000 at the 1885 composition.
Within each kaza, cluster shares were re-solved so that the kaza's Muslim, Muslim Roma and Christian totals equal the register, after the corrections listed below.

Hasköy kaza (incl. the 101-village Kırcaali nahiye, per TDV) and Yanbolu kaza: Muslims x1.378 (McCarthy). Haskovo town 38/5/57 -> 45.2/4.9/49.9; Hasköy west 55 -> 51.3 Turk; Harmanli 45 -> 41.8; Yambol town 31 -> 37.3. Haskovo oblast Bulgarians 53.8 (register only) -> 46.1 (target 42).

Dimetoka, Çirmen-Mustafapaşa, Kızılağaç and the Edirne-kaza villages: Muslims x1.378. Ortaköy 45 -> 61.1 Turk; Çirmen–Lyubimets 45 -> 56.1; Dimetoka 43 -> 50.9; Dereio/Roussa hills 50/15 -> 61.1/20.4; Edirne SE villages 38 -> 42.3. Yambol oblast 65.6 -> 60.7 (target 60).
The Straldzha villages moved from Yanbolu kaza to Karinâbâd kaza; the 1287-88 salname and FO 881/3655 treat Karinâbâd-Yanbolu as one unit.

Stara Zagora (author target): Muslims of Zağra-i Atik, Çırpan and Kızanlık x0.75 of the register. Kızanlık east 60 -> 50.0 Turk (the register alone gives about 62); Kızanlık west 35 -> 30.0; Eski Zağra town 35 -> 27.8; Çırpan 24 -> 18.6. Oblast 65.3 -> 70.7 (target 75).

Burgas (author target): Muslims of Karinâbâd, Aydos, Burgaz, Ahyolu and Misivri x0.85. Aydos villages 80 -> 75.6 Turk; Karnobat 61 -> 61.8; Burgas town 45 -> 42.3. Tırnovacık nahiye added as 24,000 Strandzha Christians out of the vilayet residual (it is missing from the 31-village Kırkkilise list). Oblast 46.7 -> 49.4 (target 54).

Smolyan: Rupçoz nahiye split into Chepelare (Smolyan oblast) and Bachkovo–Hvoyna (Plovdiv oblast); less of Darıdere's population placed in Zlatograd. Oblast 34.0 (target 38). Plovdiv 61.7 (64), Pazardzhik 71.6 (71), Sliven 65.8 (64) and Kardzhali 3.5 (3) stay at the register without calibration factors.

Thrace kazas now follow the FO 881/3655 village ratios. Uzunköprü 33 -> 26.7 Turk (its villages are only 18% Muslim); Kırkkilise town 33 -> 23.2; Pınarhisar 22 -> 13.2; Babaeski 35 -> 25.2 Turk + 9.5 Circassian/Roma; Hayrabolu 70 -> 69.8; Malkara 50 -> 48.2; Lüleburgaz 40 -> 41.9; Çorlu 45 -> 43.6; Gümülcine town 62 -> 55.9 Turk + 9.9 other; Gümülcine west plain 78 -> 64.5; Koşukavak 93 -> 89.4.
Edirne city 48/4/48 -> 36.8/6.1/57.1, 80,875 people. Basis: Belleten, 35,000 Muslims of 94,000 in 1858; the town Roma share comes from the Ubicini residual.

Drama sanjak (Selanik vilayet) now follows the 1873 register. İskeçe town 52 -> 18.4 Turk (867 Muslim of 4,720 males); Yenice-i Karasu plain 70 -> 65.5; Darıdere kaza (Zlatograd, Eğridere/Ardino, Termes) about 99% Muslim. Eğridere is 64.5 Turk / 34.7 Pomak.

Turk vs other Muslim: Pomaks, Circassians, Muslim Roma and Kıpti count as muslim_other. Circassians are Çerkezköy 70%, Kızılağaç/Doruklu 35%, Babaeski/Terzili 20% and Pınarhisar/İvanköy 15% of Muslims. Tatars, Yörüks and Kızılbaş (Roussa) count as turk. Overall 83% of the region's Muslims are Turkish.

Clusters and coordinates. Avratalan (Koprivshtitsa) split from Prasadim Derbent (Klisura). Rupçoz split into Chepelare and Bachkovo–Hvoyna. Termes–Oraio moved south to 41.31/24.90; it sat on the Bulgarian side. Echinos cluster moved to 41.23/24.96. Renamed: the Straldzha cluster (Karinâbâd western villages), the Malko Tarnovo cluster (Tırnovacık nahiye), the Büyükçekmece cluster (Makriköy dropped) and Edirne NE (the Üsküdar nahiye label dropped; that nahiye was at Shtit near Svilengrad).

Admin units added. Edirne vilayet: sancaks Filibe, İslimye, Edirne, Tekfurdağı and Gelibolu, with Ferecik–Makri and Gümülcine under Gelibolu as in FO 881/3655. Selanik/Drama: Darıdere, Yenice-i Karasu, İskeçe. İstanbul: Çatalca and Dersaadet.
